story: If you fall into a stellar black hole feet first, extreme tidal forces will stretch you vertically and compress you horizontally into a noodle before you even reach the event horizon. Gravity at your feet will pull much harder than at your head, while opposite sides of your body are squeezed inward. However, if you fall into a supermassive black hole, the story changes completely. Because supermassive black holes are so massive, their spacetime curvature at the edge is far more gentle. You could cross the event horizon entirely in one piece, noticing no immediate tidal disruption. Deep inside a supermassive black hole, falling toward the center becomes inevitable, but the immediate death by spaghettification is delayed until you venture much deeper into its interior.
angle: Falling into a supermassive black hole might allow you to cross the edge completely in one piece, whereas a small black hole turns you into a noodle before you even get inside.
